notes.title: Path to Serenity - Release Announcement!
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

I'm pleased to announce that Path to Serenity will be released on the 16th of June. It has been an incredible journey to reach this milestone, and I want to express my gratitude to everyone who has provided feedback and support along the way.

Path to Serenity will be available on Steam, Itch.io, and the Humble Store starting June 16th. For every unit sold on these platforms, I will donate $0.10 to the Safe in Our World charity.

I hope you'll enjoy Path to Serenity and its message, which is dear to my heart: finding happiness in life. For me, that means spending more time at home with my son and family, creating games, and building my studio. I believe everyone has their own path to happiness.

Thank you once again for wishlisting my game and for reading my posts.

Silviu

notes.title: Path to Serenity - Safe in Our World
notes.content:
[b]Exciting Collaboration Announcement![/b]

Hello everyone!

I am thrilled to announce a meaningful collaboration with Safe in Our World - The Video Games Mental Health Charity. For every sale of my game once it releases on Steam, Itch io and hopefully on the Humble Store (working on that!),[b] I will be donating $0.10 to their cause.[/b]

Mental health has been a personal journey for me since childhood, and supporting this cause means a lot to my solo dev studio. Path to Serenity my game does touches very slightly on themes of anxiety and the importance of spending time wisely with loved ones or pursuing passions. In the story of Jim, the protagonist, I explore how being apart from family affects his outlook, seeing the world in shades of grey and blue instead of the vibrant colours that once brought him joy.

Collaborating with this charity is a proud achievement, and I look forward to more partnerships like this in the future.

Please consider adding my game to your wishlist!

Thank you for reading my post and hope to see you at the next update! 

Silviu

notes.title: Path to Serenity - Implementing Steam Next Fest feedback
notes.content:
[b]Hey everyone![/b]

With Rise of the Village Hero now at version 1.0, I’m excited to shift my focus entirely to Path to Serenity. First, I want to say a huge thank you to everyone who played the demo during Steam Next Fest and added the game to their wishlist—your support truly means a lot to me!

I’ve been working hard to implement the feedback I received from the festival. One of the key improvements is the addition of subtitles while Jim speaks, making the game more accessible. These are still being refined, but I’m pleased with the progress so far.

I’ve also focused on improving the overall gameplay flow to create a smoother and more immersive experience. For example, I’ve added reminders to help players navigate tasks, addressing feedback about being stuck—such as in the office chair task. Additionally, I’ve introduced subtle fade-in animations to better communicate the passage of time after certain tasks, enhancing immersion.

Right now, I’m working on finalising the last level’s tasks and objectives. My next step is testing and polishing, which I anticipate will be a relatively short process. After this initial phase, I’ll likely continue adding more content before repeating the testing and refinement process.

I’m looking forward to sharing some exciting announcements soon! 

Development is progressing well, and I’m also working on enhancing the Steam page, so expect to see more gifs and improvements in the coming days.

Thanks again for your support—I really appreciate it!

[b]Silviu[/b]

notes.title: Path to Serenity Demo available till March 4th!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

I've managed to set up the demo and it's ready for you to try out. It's a bit nerve-wracking, but here it is. The demo is now live and will remain so until March 4th. I'm open to receiving feedback and will gladly make updates as needed to address any bugs or issues that are discovered with the demo.

Overall, the demo is quite short, offering about 15-20 minutes of gameplay if you explore everything, and even less if you focus strictly on the tasks and objectives.

If you enjoy my walking simulator cozy game, please consider wishlisting it on Steam. I would also appreciate any suggestions or feedback you might have. You can provide feedback by pressing F12 inside the game and filling out the feedback form. If you would like to see more of something or less of let me know. If you encounter any bugs, just indicate them in the form.

You only need to fill in the subject of your feedback and the content; you don't need to add your email if you prefer not to.

Your feedback means a lot to me. Thank you for your patience, and I hope you enjoy playing the demo!

The demo will be available for the Steam next fest as well up untill 4th March so quite a bit of time to try it out. 

Thank you again for your support.

Silviu

notes.title: Happy New Year! Wishing you all a great 2025!
notes.content:
Happy New Year!

I can hardly believe it’s been a year already. 2025 is here! This journey began in 2023, and on 13th January 2024, I released [b]Rise of the Village Hero[/b]. Nearly a year later, I’m continuing to release monthly updates for Rise of the Village Hero while also making progress on [b]Path to Serenity[/b].

As I’m currently on holiday (returning 8th January), I wanted to take a moment to thank you all for your incredible support. I wish you the very best for 2025—may all your plans and dreams come true! I hope you’ve enjoyed a wonderful holiday season surrounded by family and friends.

Looking ahead to 2025, here’s what’s in store:
•	[b]Rise of the Village Hero[/b]: I’ll keep releasing monthly updates as I work towards the full 1.0 release. If you haven’t already, check out the free demo—it’s a great way to see if the game’s for you. And don’t miss the final hours of the 35% off sale—it’s a great time to grab the game!
•	[b]Path to Serenity[/b]: I’m aiming to release the game as soon as it’s ready. For updates, follow me on X (formerly Twitter), Bluesky, or join my Discord. Don’t forget to wishlist the game on Steam—it really helps!
•	[b]Prototyping[/b]: After completing Path to Serenity and reaching 1.0 with Rise of the Village Hero, I’ll be exploring ideas for my third game.


[b]Thank you so much for being part of this journey. As a solo developer, your support truly means the world to me.


Here’s to an amazing 2025! See you in the next update.[/b]

Silviu

notes.title: Devlog 1 - More interactions, expansion of levels, polish and Kickstarter
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Welcome to Devlog 1! I’ll aim to keep these posts regular, at least once a month. Here’s what I’ve been working on this month for Path to Serenity:

I’m continuing to add more interactions to the world. I’ve built a flexible system that allows me to reuse the same scripts to create tasks, objectives, and interactive items. This month, I’ve focused on adding more of these elements to enhance the story and provide players with a deeper understanding of what’s happening. Path to Serenity is all about exploration—completing tasks by interacting with objects, and this is a key aspect of the game’s design.

I’ve added new interactive elements to the office scene:

A resignation letter from a staff member, Ewan, which the boss crumples, showing his lack of care.
A letter turned into an airplane, where the boss asks everyone to work hard and promises a pizza party on Friday.
A letter from Aunt Didi, now on the player’s desk, which reflects the protagonist’s struggles.
I’ve also been polishing the level design to make sure the environments look and feel as good as possible. I’ve been experimenting with post-processing effects and lighting to fine-tune the scenes.
More audio recordings of me voicing the main character have also been added as well as more sound effects. 

In terms of tasks, I’ve been reorganising them to add more variety and depth. Now that the main mechanics are in place, it’s all about refining them and telling the story in the way I’ve envisioned.

Next, I’ll be focusing on creating a fourth level—a night scene in the forest. This will take place after the player leaves the office and gets lost on the road.

Many of the core mechanics are already in place, but there’s still work to be done. For example, controller support is already functional, but I need to ensure it works smoothly with the menus as well—currently, it’s only partial. If I cant get it to work the game will only work partially with the controller. But I am still working on it. There are also plans to add more options to the menu, such as credits and audio settings.

It’s going to be a busy month, but I’m looking forward to the progress!

I also wanted to share that Path to Serenity is now got a page that is live on Kickstarter. This campaign will help me bring in more unique art and really improve the game’s visual quality should the funding levels be reached. If you’d like to support it, I’ll leave a link below:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/luduspaxstudios/path-to-serenity-a-tranquil-adventure

Thank you for your consideration, and I look forward to seeing you in the next devlog, where I’ll discuss what I’ve achieved and what’s coming next.

Silviu
